title: Binary Tree Preorder Traversal
summary: Given the root node of a binary tree, provide the values of its nodes in a preorder traversal sequence.
statement: Given the root node of a binary tree, provide the values of its nodes in a preorder traversal sequence.
constraints: The tree has 0–100 nodes; -100 <= node.val <= 100. It is not necessarily a binary search tree.
Visit each node in root → left subtree → right subtree order. Return a flat list of values, retaining duplicates. An empty tree returns [].

hints: Treat a subtree as a smaller copy of the same traversal problem.
A missing node does nothing. For a present node, perform root → left subtree → right subtree in that order.
Use one shared result list and a helper for a node; append its value at the required position among the two recursive calls.
Values are not necessarily sorted. Structure and the visit order, not numerical magnitude, determine the result.
editorial: Apply root → left subtree → right subtree recursively at every node, doing nothing at a missing child. A shared output list avoids repeatedly copying subtree lists. Each node is appended once; recursion requires O(h) stack space, where h is height. At most 100 nodes keeps this reference within ordinary Python recursion limits. An explicit-stack implementation is also valid. The independent oracle never calls this traversal: it maps JSON nodes to binary position paths and sorts symbolic ordering keys.
